question: And what does a device do when it sleeps?
why_it_blocks: answered before the question door existed; migrated into the corpus so the system reads its Q&A in one place
answer: ok, so ground loop is sending everybody a pulse periodically. while most of the system is an event driven one. so as an example: at, say, 2300 cairn might kick off sleep, by running his sleep routine. then over the bus he turns the sleep token over to the next system and so on. librarian will have real sleep. memory consolidation. the learning blocks will have the same, tho maybe not as big a task since their memory set will be inherently smaller. the system device might do backups or run periodic SSD checks. what each device does depends on the device. the word graph based embeddings generating device won't need to do anything i don't think. but cairn will have a lot to do. it's cairn's job to clean out the logging tree of things older than 30 days.
